sources.note: Igana not yet recorded in 1971 (Tamolan = Itutang, Midsivindi, Akrukay, Breri, Romkun). Tamolan typological notes (sec. 2.23.22.3, p.82) are segmental only ('Romkun is possibly tonal'); survey-wide disclaimer p.7 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.'

sources.note: Igana only in the Keram-Ramu family tree (fig. 1.7, 'East Iski' with Kominimung) and table 1.16 ('igg igan1243 Igana, Wasmuk, Iski'); no data.

sources.citation: Brooks, Joseph D. 2018. Realis and irrealis: Chini verb morphology, clause chaining, and discourse. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Nothing on Igana stress; states the documentation situation: p.70 fn.34 'Z'graggen does not include a single transcribed word from either [Kominimung, Igana] in his (1974) wordlist'; p.71 'For Kominimung and Igana, also purported to be Ramu languages, no data are available.'

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2005. Linguistic prehistory in the Sepik-Ramu basin. In Pawley et al. (eds.), Papuan Pasts, 109-144. Pacific Linguistics 572.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tamolan family assigned to Lower Ramu on Akrukay evidence; no Igana data, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. & J. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 731-763. Pacific Linguistics C-38.

sources.note: Igana appears only in the Tamolan Family population table (p.740, 'Igana 114?'); Ramu Super-Stock comments (pp.758-760) exemplify Kambot only; nothing on Igana phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-B41

sources.note: Nothing. p.4: 'Short wordlists only were collected . M10 Kominimung and M11 Igana; they were however enough for a linguistic classification.' p.35: gazetteer 'M11 Igana 114 (Wasmuk)'. Classification and census only.
